AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To develop a risk scoring system (RSS) for predicting recurrence in women with borderline ovarian tumours (BOTs).

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Cohort study of women with BOTs.

AbstractText.Label: POPULATION
AbstractText.content: A cohort of 360 women with BOTs who received primary surgical treatment between January 2000 and December 2013.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Clinical and pathological factors affecting recurrence in women with BOTs.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE
AbstractText.content: The development of a model for the prediction of recurrence in women with BOTs.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Overall the recurrence rate was 20.0% (72/360). Recurrence was associated with five variables: age < 45 years; preoperative serum tumour marker CA125 > 150 IU/mL; a serous histological subtype; International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage other than IA; and ovarian surgery other than bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO; i.e. cystectomy and unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy). These variables were included in the RSS and assigned scores ranging from 0 to 6. The discrimination of the RSS was 0.82 (95% confidence interval, 95% CI 0.79-0.85). A total score of 8 points corresponded to the optimal threshold of the RSS, with a rate of recurrence of 11.8% (35/297) and 58.7% (37/63) for women at low risk (<8 points) and women at high risk (≥8 points), respectively. The diagnostic accuracy was 85.0%.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: This study shows that the risk of BOT recurrence can be accurately predicted so that women at high risk can benefit from adapted surgical treatment.

AbstractText.Label: TWEETABLE ABSTRACT
AbstractText.content: Our RSS permitted women with BOTs at low risk to be distinguished from women with BOTs at high risk of recurrence.
